narrative.overview: The site's one idea: a backend engineer's credentials don't sit in a list, they cross like independently-tensioned silk bands, and where they overlap, the browser computes a real color that never exists in the palette on its own — a mix-blend-mode: multiply result, not a precomputed image. The band strip itself is a pure visual signature with no text on it at all; directly beneath it, in normal document flow, sit the two most enticing credentials (the internship, the solo-shipped platform). Splitting mechanism from proof this way was a finish-review correction: text overlaid on a diagonal, multiply-blended shape kept drifting outside its own bounds. This replaces a prior glassmorphism template that read as generic AI-portfolio default; the new system refuses every trace of it: no blur-as-decoration, no rounded corners, no drop shadows. Depth comes from color layering, not elevation tokens.
keyCharacteristics: Depth via live-computed color overlap (mix-blend-mode: multiply), never shadows or glass
Square corners everywhere — zero border-radius, no exceptions
Geist Sans for every display/body voice; Geist Mono exclusively for labels, tags, and credential metadata
One authored entrance (bands sweep in and settle once); no scattered hover gimmicks
Every color has a job tied to a real credential domain, never decorative

rules.name: The Computed-Not-Painted Rule
rules.body: Any color representing an overlap between two credential domains must be produced by real mix-blend-mode composition in the browser, never picked by eye and hardcoded as a flat fill.

rules.name: The One Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: Sun-White is the only background color on the page outside the band composition itself. No section gets a tinted panel.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No heading is ever preceded by a numbered or labeled kicker. The heading carries its own weight.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is used only for labels, tags, and metadata — never for headings or body prose, and never reached for 'to look technical.'

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and stay flat on hover — no lifting, no shadow-on-hover. Interactive response is a color shift only.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Every rendered element uses zero border-radius. No exceptions in the shipped surface.

rules.name: The Alternating Column Rule
rules.body: Every section from Skills onward alternates which side of the container its heading and primary content column sit against: Skills (right), Record (left), Contact (right). Structured data inside a right-aligned section keeps its own internal left-to-right reading order. The starting side flipped once at the user's request — 'alternate' is the invariant, not which side starts.

rules.name: The Text-Off-The-Bands Rule
rules.body: The band strip carries no text. Credentials live in a normal-flow row beneath it, never overlaid on the diagonal shapes — an earlier version anchored captions to the bands and they kept drifting outside the shape at different viewports.

rules.name: The Value-First Rule
rules.body: In the Contact link list, value/label/icon form one tight cluster (gap-3) pushed as a whole to the far right (ml-auto) — left to right inside the cluster: value, label, icon, so reading from the row's right edge inward gives icon then label then value. The CV download sits below the link list, never beside it.

dos: Do compute every credential-overlap color live via mix-blend-mode: multiply; never hardcode a flat fill as a stand-in for an overlap that should be computed.
Do keep every corner square (0px radius) — buttons, cards, chips, images, everything.
Do reserve Geist Mono for labels, tags, and data; keep headings and body prose in Geist Sans.
Do cap display type at 6rem regardless of viewport.
Do tie every color to a real credential domain rather than using them decoratively.
donts: Don't overlay text directly on the band strip's diagonal shapes — credentials live in the normal-flow row beneath it.
Don't use Saffron as text color on Sun-White; use Saffron Ink (#8f631a) instead.
Don't add a kicker, eyebrow, or numbered label above any section heading.
Don't add drop shadows, glassmorphism, or blur-as-decoration anywhere.
Don't use a Unicode arrow or emoji glyph as a stand-in icon; use a real icon component or plain text.
Don't introduce a fourth accent color without checking whether it can be expressed as a computed overlap of the existing three.
